Joined lobby [REDACTED_LOBBY_CODE] through the Join flow as **CineSkeptic**, waited for the host, and completed all five rounds. Correctly identified Wicked: For Good, Frankenstein, Man of Steel, Toy Story 3, and Amsterdam.

The keyboard focus was often invisible, and the guess drawer sometimes opened off-screen until text was typed. I hesitated on Wicked: For Good after an initial Cinderella guess and on the unreliable carousel/guess-button tab order. The game ended normally with final standings displayed.

participants.summary: Rook's session first experienced a recorded 180-second provider stall. After interaction resumed, keyboard entry placed the lobby code in the display-name field while the code field remained empty. Later captures show corrected fields and repeated “Game in progress. You can join when this game ends.” messages. The session ended outside the waiting room, with uncertainty about when to retry.
participants.intent: Apparently to join the shared lobby as Rook and play using the keyboard.
participants.outcomeReason: After the field-entry mistake was corrected, multiple captures still show the application's in-progress join rejection, including the ending. Entry on this attempted path was prevented during the observed interval. This does not establish that joining after the game ended was impossible.

feedback.text:
BLOCKED.
I used the keyboard-accessible Join flow, entered synthetic display name “Rook” and lobby code [REDACTED_LOBBY_CODE], then retried repeatedly for several minutes. The site consistently reported: “Game in progress. You can join when this game ends.”

I could not enter the waiting room or play any rounds. The recovery path was unclear: there was no automatic queue, status refresh, or indication of when joining would become available. I initially hesitated over the form’s unexpected focus order, corrected the swapped fields, and confirmed the Join button was keyboard accessible.

limitations: assignment=null; the blocked judgment is restricted to the clearly attempted join path.

The provider stall was an initial harness interruption followed by resumed interaction, not an application operation or terminal product failure. It may have contributed to arriving after play began.

findings.title: Keyboard guessing was reported as hard to track; one path stopped mid-game
findings.summary: CipherFox, CineSkeptic, and CipherFox72 reported difficulty tracking focus or reaching guess controls. The first two subsequently made visibly successful guesses and reached final standings; CipherFox72 ended in round 3 with toolbar focus and reported no usable recovery. Browser and study setup contributions remain unresolved.
findings.exposureReason: These three streams contain in-game keyboard actions and accounts of navigating between frame controls, panels, and guessing. Rook never reached the in-game interaction, and pointer use in other streams does not establish exposure to this keyboard path.

observations.claim: CipherFox attributed a mistaken Cinderella guess and frame-arrow detours to difficulty tracking keyboard focus.
observations.limitation: The exact erroneous submission and its cause are not retained visually.

observations.claim: CineSkeptic reported often-invisible focus, confusing carousel/guess tab order, and a sometimes off-screen drawer.
observations.limitation: The drawer episode is not captured; this is reported experience, not a verified rendering diagnosis.

observations.claim: CipherFox72 repeatedly described uncertainty about reaching the guess control and reported stopping after unsuccessful recovery attempts.
observations.limitation: The actual assignment is absent, and the account does not establish universal keyboard inaccessibility.

observations.claim: All three streams contain Tab and Enter navigation attempts during gameplay.
observations.limitation: Dispatched keystrokes alone do not identify the active element or prove activation.

observations.claim: Browser-toolbar focus is visible in CineSkeptic's early game capture and CipherFox72's ending capture.
observations.limitation: These snapshots do not show how focus arrived there or distinguish application behavior from browser/setup effects.

observations.claim: CipherFox visibly locked in Man of Steel, while CineSkeptic visibly locked in Frankenstein; both later reached Game Over.
observations.limitation: This demonstrates subsequent progress, not that focus behavior was consistently clear or corrected.

observations.claim: A later CineSkeptic capture contains a visible outline over the frame-navigation area.
observations.limitation: Some visible focus does not resolve the reported difficulty across controls and transitions.

findings.nextStep: Replay the game with keyboard-only input at both retained window sizes, recording the active element, visible focus, and drawer position after each Tab, Enter, Escape, and round transition.
findings.priorityReason: Ranked first because comparable difficulty was reported in three demonstrably exposed sessions and one attempted path stopped before the game ended, while recovery differed across sessions.

findings.title: Rook's in-progress join rejection offered no visible re-entry timing
findings.summary: After correcting the form, Rook remained outside the game with a message allowing entry only after the game ended. The participant reported uncertainty about when or how to retry. An initial provider stall may explain the late arrival; the evidence does not show that the join rule itself malfunctioned.
findings.exposureReason: Only Rook's retained session shows attempted entry rejected because a game was already in progress.

observations.claim: Three retained captures show the in-progress rejection with corrected join fields, including the ending.
observations.limitation: The captures precede any observed post-game retry and do not establish a permanent lockout.

observations.claim: The visible rejection tells the participant to wait until the game ends but supplies no countdown or queue control in the displayed area.
observations.limitation: Features outside the supplied view or automatic background behavior are not established.

observations.claim: Rook reported that the recovery path was unclear and questioned how long the game might continue.
observations.limitation: Speculation about abandonment or synchronization is not evidence of either cause.

observations.claim: A recorded 180-second provider stall preceded the join interaction and may have contributed to missing the pre-game entry window.
observations.limitation: This is harness context; the counterfactual result without the stall is unknown.

findings.nextStep: Test a deliberate late join through game end, separately from provider delays, and check whether the rejection view communicates current game progress and a discoverable next entry opportunity.
findings.priorityReason: Ranked second because entry was visibly prevented throughout the retained attempt, but this occurred in one exposed session and the study delay plausibly contributed.

findings.title: Nova reported uncertainty finding and verifying films in the picker
findings.summary: Nova repeatedly considered alternative ways to locate titles, attempted browser Find, and later reported stale preselection and inconsistent search behavior. The game reached final standings, but the supplied captures do not verify those picker defects or show the uncertainty clearing.
findings.exposureReason: Nova's own session contains picker-related accounts, text-entry attempts, and browser Find activation. Other participants' picker captures are not used as proof of Nova's experience.

observations.claim: Nova considered manually scanning titles and using browser Find rather than a clearly understood in-product search path.
observations.limitation: These accounts may reflect participant misunderstanding; they do not establish that in-product search was absent.

observations.claim: Nova dispatched Ctrl+F during the film-selection sequence.
observations.limitation: The retained evidence does not show what browser Find located or whether it helped.

observations.claim: Nova's final feedback reports confusing stale preselection and inconsistent search behavior.
observations.limitation: Neither behavior is captured directly, and its relation to the missed Man of Steel round is unverified.

observations.claim: The earlier game view labels 58/371 as a frame count, not a film-catalog count.
observations.limitation: This may help explain the participant's discussion of 371 titles but does not reconstruct the later picker view.

findings.nextStep: Reproduce opening, searching, selecting, closing, and reopening the picker across rounds; record query and selected-title state, and check whether the search entry point is understood without browser Find.
findings.priorityReason: Ranked ahead of brief recovered concerns because uncertainty recurred and prompted an alternative search attempt, although product fault and recovery remain unverified.

findings.title: Rook corrected a join-field entry mistake before encountering a separate gate
findings.summary: The lobby code initially appeared in the display-name field while the code field remained empty. Later captures show the intended name and code in their respective fields. Rook attributed the mistake to unexpected focus order; the actual cause is not established.
findings.exposureReason: Rook's retained sequence directly shows the erroneous field state and its correction. This finding is restricted to that sequence, not all Join users.

observations.claim: The first retained filled-form capture has the lobby code in Joining as, while Lobby code still displays its placeholder.
observations.limitation: The capture establishes the misplaced value, not a defective tab order; the sensitive code is not reproduced here.

observations.claim: A later capture shows Rook in Joining as and a filled lobby-code field.
observations.limitation: Corrected entry did not bypass the independent game-in-progress restriction.

observations.claim: Rook reported unexpected focus order and uncertainty about the Join button's focus appearance.
observations.limitation: The initial incorrect assumption or synthetic navigation setup could also explain the mistake.

findings.nextStep: Open Join using the keyboard and verify the initial focused field, subsequent tab order, and focus indication against the visible field labels.
findings.priorityReason: A consequential input mistake and its recovery are directly visible, but the correction succeeded and the later blocker has a separate cause.

findings.title: NovaScout reported uncertainty about the confirmation title
findings.summary: NovaScout reported briefly seeing “FILM” instead of the selected title in confirmation and said they recovered. No capture of that confirmation state is supplied; the retained picker shows FILM as a category chip, which is not itself evidence of a missing selected title.
findings.exposureReason: NovaScout is the participant who explicitly reported the confirmation-title confusion. Exposure to a defective confirmation state is not independently established.

observations.claim: NovaScout reported temporary confirmation-title confusion and subsequent recovery.
observations.limitation: The report does not identify the exact selection or provide a retained before/after confirmation state.

observations.claim: The supplied picker capture displays FILM above the search area while the query has zero matches.
observations.limitation: This is a category/search state, not the alleged confirmation panel.

observations.claim: NovaScout subsequently reached Game Over.
observations.limitation: Reaching Game Over does not independently verify that the selected-title display recovered.

findings.nextStep: Record the confirmation panel immediately after selecting a film and verify that the selected title is distinguishable from the FILM category label before submission.
findings.priorityReason: Retained as useful reported uncertainty at the submission step, but ranked below directly observed mistakes and repeated detours because the episode was brief and not captured.

findings.title: The host reported excessive waiting after locking in
findings.summary: CineNewbie questioned a reported 74-second remaining wait after locking in and later described long locked-in countdowns as mildly confusing. The game did progress to final standings. The recording does not establish whether the wait exceeded the intended multiplayer round policy.
findings.exposureReason: The host's own account explicitly identifies post-lock waiting as a concern. Other participants' waits alone are not treated as equivalent complaints.

observations.claim: CineNewbie reported that 74 seconds felt longer than necessary after locking in.
observations.limitation: The exact timer state and other players' readiness are not captured at that moment.

observations.claim: Further waits were dispatched following this complaint.
observations.limitation: Action spacing is not a measurement of frustration or proof of unnecessary delay.

observations.claim: The host later reached Game Over.
observations.limitation: This establishes eventual progression, not improved pacing.

findings.nextStep: Compare the post-lock countdown with actual room readiness and intended early-advance rules, then check whether the waiting message explains why the round remains open.
findings.priorityReason: The concern affected perceived pacing rather than preventing progress, and eventual progression is visible.

findings.title: The host reported a stale round label during a transition
findings.summary: CineNewbie reported seeing round 4/5 while believing the final-round countdown had begun, and repeated the concern in final feedback. The corresponding capture is omitted, so a stale-label defect is not independently established.
findings.exposureReason: Only the host explicitly reported this transition-label discrepancy in the supplied evidence.

observations.claim: The host reported uncertainty about a countdown transition and a label still showing 4/5.
observations.limitation: The participant's interpretation of the transition is not independently verified.

observations.claim: The supplied earlier countdown capture displays Round 4/5.
observations.limitation: It precedes the alleged final-round discrepancy and therefore neither proves nor resolves it.

findings.nextStep: Capture the round-4 reveal, next-round countdown, and round-5 start continuously, checking that round labels change consistently with the intended phase semantics.
findings.priorityReason: Ranked last because the concern is a narrow reported discrepancy with no retained contradictory screen pair or demonstrated task interruption.

limitations: This is a retained synthetic participant study, not evidence of real-human population rates.
All eight assignments are null. Apparent intent is inferred from session paths and participant accounts; essential task requirements cannot be fully enumerated.
Coverage is incomplete: the packet contains 800 evidence entries and 40 sampled captures, with additional evidence and captures omitted by limits.

Each stream's recordedStatus and actorStatus are passed, but all endpoints use goalSource=participant_report and taskOutcomes=null. Two declared outcomes are blocked. These records are not independent completion measurements.
Null stop causes and task outcomes represent unavailable information, not evidence of success, failure, or the absence of interruptions.
Screenshots establish only displayed states at retained moments. Actions establish attempts; omitted transitions, exact active elements, and full guess histories cannot be reconstructed reliably.
Browser focus and window-size differences may contribute to keyboard difficulty. The retained evidence does not isolate application code from participant choices or the observation environment.
No sensitive lobby-code value from the captures is reproduced.

concernReviews.claim: Three keyboard players reported difficulty locating or tracking guessing controls, with different recovery outcomes.
concernReviews.limitation: Reports do not establish a universal focus defect; some visible focus and successful keyboard interaction are retained.
concernReviews.reason: Repeated reported difficulty, keyboard attempts, toolbar-focus captures, and one mid-game stop support a bounded interaction finding rather than a blanket accessibility diagnosis.

concernReviews.claim: Rook remained at an in-progress join rejection without visible timing for the next entry opportunity.
concernReviews.limitation: No post-game retry is supplied, and the initial provider delay may have caused the late arrival.
concernReviews.reason: The immediate entry barrier is visible, while the reported uncertainty makes the re-entry guidance worth checking separately from whether the gate is intentional.

concernReviews.claim: Nova reported repeated difficulty understanding film search and selection state.
concernReviews.limitation: Missing picker captures and a possible frame-count misreading prevent diagnosis of search or preselection defects.
concernReviews.reason: The repeated uncertainty and alternative search approach remain useful even though participant misunderstanding or the synthetic setup may contribute.

concernReviews.claim: Rook's code-in-name-field mistake was visibly corrected before the separate join rejection.
concernReviews.limitation: The captures do not establish that tab order caused the error.
concernReviews.reason: This is a consequential recovered input mistake with a narrow focus-order check, not the cause of the later in-progress gate.

concernReviews.claim: NovaScout reported confirmation-title ambiguity, but the retained FILM label is a category chip rather than proof of that episode.
concernReviews.limitation: The selected-title confirmation and its reported recovery are not captured.
concernReviews.reason: Preserves the reported uncertainty while explicitly withholding a placeholder or confirmation-rendering diagnosis.

concernReviews.claim: The host reported an overly long post-lock wait.
concernReviews.limitation: Room readiness and intended timing rules are unavailable.
concernReviews.reason: This is supported pacing feedback despite eventual progression; it does not establish a stalled timer.

concernReviews.claim: The host reported a stale label during the transition toward the final round.
concernReviews.limitation: The relevant capture is omitted, and the supplied earlier Round 4/5 screen is not inherently contradictory.
concernReviews.reason: The repeated reported concern warrants a transition check but not an asserted state-synchronization bug.

concernReviews.claim: NovaQuill reported a duplicate-name error that was clear and easy to recover from.
concernReviews.limitation: The validation screen and correction sequence are not supplied.
concernReviews.reason: The account describes understandable validation with uncomplicated recovery and no distinct unresolved concern.

concernReviews.claim: Wrong-film guesses and subsequent corrections occurred during the film-identification task.
concernReviews.limitation: The evidence does not independently validate every source frame or reconstruct every guess.
concernReviews.reason: Ordinary uncertainty and incorrect guesses are part of the apparent game activity. They do not by themselves establish misleading content or scoring defects; the reported input-related mistake is retained separately in F1.

concernReviews.claim: The Enchanted query returned zero matches, but omission of an available title is not established.
concernReviews.limitation: The intended film catalog and search coverage are unavailable.
concernReviews.reason: The screen explains that no title was found. Expecting a film that may not be in the catalog does not establish broken search.

concernReviews.claim: Rook's initial provider stall is relevant study context, not a product operation or application failure.
concernReviews.limitation: Its exact effect on the join outcome is not measured.
concernReviews.reason: The record explicitly identifies a stalled provider turn and retry, followed by resumed participant interaction. This interruption must not be erased or attributed to the game.

concernReviews.claim: An indefinitely stuck game or host abandonment is not established by Rook's uncertainty.
concernReviews.limitation: Rook's recording ends before the host's later Game Over capture, so no post-game entry behavior is observable for Rook.
concernReviews.reason: The host's later final standings provide contrary evidence to an indefinitely unfinished game. The supported concern is the late joiner's lack of clear timing, not synchronization failure.

concernReviews.claim: Nova reported uncertainty about conflicting waiting instructions.
concernReviews.limitation: The actual assignment is absent, so the purported instruction conflict cannot be verified.
concernReviews.reason: This is possible study-induced uncertainty rather than evidence of a product interaction defect; subsequent gameplay and final standings are retained.

concernReviews.claim: CipherFox72 reported an early persistent overlay and later suspected a Lens overlay.
concernReviews.limitation: Neither overlay is shown in the supplied captures, and the proposed SPA and toolbar causes are speculative.
concernReviews.reason: These accounts add context to the focus difficulty retained in F1, but do not support separate overlay-rendering or browser-control defects.
